schema.gdv_fields: the Game Design Vector: field id, label, and the default written when no evidence speaks to it; scope marks a default that repeats a scope line, which the owner holds
schema.axis_rules: per bipolar axis, per pole: the design signal, the design consequence, GDV field values, negative constraints and prophecy lines
schema.weight_rules: per weight: what high attraction implies, and the constraint implied by a clear aversion
schema.contradictions: pairs of signals in tension and the design that resolves them productively; a and b are dimension ids with + or -
schema.fantasies: central-fantasy sentences keyed by the leading reward weight
schema.core_verbs: core verb phrases keyed by the leading solve, conflict or reward weight
schema.scope: the pocket-game lines written into every build prompt: summary is the line above them, constraints are held by the owner and may be changed by the owner, fixed are not open at all

neg.signal: wants to be pointed at something worth doing
neg.implication: Give one clear, always-visible current objective and let the player trust it. Announce optional content as optional. The game never leaves the player wondering what it wants.

gdv.progression_structure: an authored sequence of clear objectives, one at a time
gdv.explicit_instruction: moderate: the current objective is always stated in the world

negative: Do not open with an undirected sandbox.
visions: I see a hand that points, once, and you go where it points and are glad of it.

pos.signal: sets their own goals and resists being told
pos.implication: Provide tools and a place, not a to-do list. Objectives exist as things in the world the player may adopt, ignore or replace, and the game notices and rewards goals the player set for themselves.

gdv.progression_structure: player-chosen goals in an open structure; authored goals are offers, not orders

negative: No mandatory quest log.
Do not make progress depend on obeying an instruction.
visions: I see no quest log.
You will be told where to go. You will go somewhere else, and find the game was waiting there.

neg.signal: keeps moving toward the next new thing
neg.implication: Keep introducing new situations. No mechanic outstays its welcome; prefer short arcs of novelty over deep refinement of one system.

gdv.reward_schedule: frequent novelty: a new space, rule or object every few minutes
gdv.replayability: breadth: different things to find on another visit

negative: Do not repeat a challenge more than twice without changing it.
visions: I see a place you have never visited, but will recognise immediately.

pos.signal: enjoys perfecting a system once it is understood
pos.implication: Build around one core system with real depth. Let skill grow visibly; repeat situations with variation so that improvement is felt.

gdv.mechanical_complexity: one deep system rather than many shallow ones
gdv.replayability: mastery: the same challenge, done better

negative: Do not dilute the core mechanic with one-off gimmicks.
visions: You will do the same thing forty times, and the fortieth will be beautiful.

neg.signal: gathers information and prepares before acting
neg.implication: Make information available before commitment: situations can be scouted, threats can be read, and there is time to think. Reward preparation.

gdv.hidden_information: moderate: what matters can be learned by looking first

negative: Do not ambush the player with unreadable threats.
visions: I see you standing at the edge of something, counting, long before you step.

pos.signal: commits with incomplete information and adapts
pos.implication: Throw the player into situations with partial information and make recovery the fun. Keep commitment cheap and adaptation rich.

gdv.randomness: moderate: situations vary so plans cannot be memorised

negative: Do not require long planning phases before play.
visions: You will be halfway across before you ask whether it holds.

neg.implication: Make safety a valid and satisfying strategy. Never force a gamble; careful play may be slower but it must work.

gdv.difficulty_philosophy: fair and readable; danger is opt-in

negative: Do not force irreversible gambles on the critical path.
visions: I see a safe way round, and you take it, and it is still an adventure.

pos.signal: pokes the dangerous thing to see what it does
pos.implication: Fill the world with tempting, obviously risky things to interact with. Curiosity is rewarded with surprise far more often than it is punished.
negative: Do not punish experimentation with heavy loss.
visions: There will be a button marked NO. You know what you will do.

neg.implication: Failure is rare, gentle and never deletes progress: soft fail states, generous checkpoints, undo where possible. Difficulty comes from thinking, not from punishment.

gdv.failure_cost: very low: no lost progress; setbacks are events in the world, not resets

negative: Avoid repeated-death loops.
Never delete more than a minute of progress.
visions: I see you never once sent back to the beginning.

pos.implication: Allow frequent recoverable failure with rapid restart. Each death teaches a rule. Never delete large amounts of progress.

gdv.failure_cost: seconds: instant retry at the point of failure
gdv.difficulty_philosophy: hard but legible: every failure names its cause
gdv.learning_style: learn by failing and reading why

negative: No long reload or walk back after a failure.
visions: I see you dying three times at the same door, and smiling on the fourth.
You will fail. You will return. This time you will know why.

neg.signal: wants nothing between them and the next thing
neg.implication: Remove waiting, backtracking and busywork. Movement is fast, rewards arrive promptly, and nothing is padded.

gdv.reward_schedule: prompt: effort and payoff are seconds apart

negative: No grinding.
No slow traversal across empty space.
visions: I see nothing standing between you and the next thing.

pos.signal: enjoys a reward that was earned
pos.implication: Let rewards be earned: effortful traversal, scarce resources and delayed payoffs are part of the pleasure, provided the effort is legible and the payoff real.

gdv.reward_schedule: sparse and earned: fewer, larger payoffs

negative: Do not hand out rewards for free.
visions: I see a long climb, and you would not have it shortened.

neg.implication: Two or three mechanics, each expressive. Depth comes from situation and combination, not from adding systems.

gdv.control_complexity: simple: move plus one or two actions

negative: No skill trees, crafting menus or stat screens.
visions: I see three things you can do, and no fourth, and it is enough.

pos.implication: Several systems that interact in ways the player can discover and exploit. Emergent solutions should be possible and should feel found, not given.

gdv.systemic_interaction: high: rules combine to produce unscripted results

negative: Do not solve problems with single-purpose keys.
visions: I see small rules leaning on each other until something unexpected falls out.

neg.implication: State goals and rules plainly. Give readable feedback for every action. The player should always know what the game wants and why something happened.

gdv.explicit_instruction: clear: short in-world instruction and readable feedback

negative: Do not hide the rules of the core mechanic.
visions: I see every door labelled, and you are grateful.

pos.signal: prefers to work out the rules alone
pos.implication: Do not explain. No tutorial text. Rules are discoverable through consistent behaviour, and there are real gaps in the map and in the story.

gdv.explicit_instruction: none: the world does not explain itself
gdv.hidden_information: high: rules and spaces are found, not given

negative: No tutorial pop-ups.
No objective markers.
visions: I see a world that does not explain itself to you.
I see a map whose edges are lies.

neg.implication: Make the efficient line visible and satisfying: clear costs, clear payoffs, and a best route that is worth finding.
negative: Do not make the optimal play feel arbitrary.
visions: I see you finding the shortest line through it, and taking it.

pos.signal: chooses the expressive option over the optimal one
pos.implication: Make the stylish, funny or personal choice mechanically legitimate. Expressive options exist, the world notices them, and they are never strictly worse.

gdv.customization: yes: the player marks the world or themselves, and the world responds

negative: Never punish the expressive choice with a worse outcome.
visions: I see you choosing the useless, splendid thing, and the world treating you accordingly.

neg.implication: Avoid mandatory dialogue sequences. Convey world information spatially and mechanically. Characters may exist, but interaction should rarely stop play.
negative: No unskippable cutscenes or dialogue.
visions: I see no one stopping you to talk.

pos.signal: plays toward people and what happens next
pos.implication: Give play a story spine: people who want things, events that follow from what the player did, and a revelation worth playing toward.
negative: Do not ship a game with no one in it and nothing at stake.
visions: I see someone with a letter, waiting for you in particular.

neg.signal: lingers where the game lets them
neg.implication: Leave room: quiet stretches, places to stop, and no timers on the critical path.

gdv.pacing: contemplative: low event density, room to look

negative: No countdown timers on the critical path.
visions: I see a room that wants nothing from you, and you stay.

pos.implication: High decision density: something to do every few seconds, short gaps, quick escalation.

gdv.pacing: brisk to relentless: a decision every few seconds
gdv.session_length: 5 to 10 minutes for a complete run

negative: No long quiet stretches without a decision.
visions: I see no quiet rooms.

neg.implication: Complete arcs in a few minutes. The game can be put down at any time without loss.
negative: Do not require one long unbroken sitting.
visions: I see something whole that fits in the time it takes a kettle to boil.

pos.implication: One continuous investment that grows across the whole session. Things planted early pay off late.
negative: Do not reset the player's investment between sections.
visions: I see something small you will carry the whole way, and what it becomes.

neg.signal: takes the route to the goal
neg.implication: Keep the critical path legible and brisk. Optional content is short, adjacent and announced.

gdv.exploration_density: low: a clear route with a few adjacent optional beats

negative: Do not hide required progress off the main route.
visions: There will be a door marked EXIT, and you will be right to take it.

pos.implication: The world contains optional spaces with mechanically meaningful discoveries. Main progression stays visible enough that wandering feels voluntary rather than caused by confusion.

gdv.exploration_density: high: optional rooms, secrets, and backtracking that pays

negative: No empty optional rooms.
visions: There will be a door marked EXIT. You will walk past it.
I see something you were never meant to reach.

neg.implication: The player is fragile. Tension comes from avoiding, hiding and escaping. Do not hand them a weapon that solves it.

gdv.difficulty_philosophy: the threat is real and the player is weak; survival is cleverness

negative: Do not make the player overpowered.
visions: I see something in the dark behind you, and you would not have it removed.

pos.implication: Let capability grow and be felt: by the end the player does easily what was impossible at the start.

gdv.progression_structure: growing capability: new powers that change what is possible

negative: Do not keep the player weak for the whole game.
visions: You will be given a weapon. You will immediately wonder what else it can cut.

neg.implication: Experiments are cheap to undo: resets, rewinds or forgiving state, so the player can try things freely.

gdv.permanence: low: state can be reset or rewound

negative: No permanently missable content.
visions: I see you trying everything, because nothing is ever truly lost.

pos.implication: Choices stay made. The world remembers and shows it: closed doors stay closed and characters recall what was done.

gdv.permanence: high: persistent world changes, no undo
gdv.ending_structure: the ending reflects the choices that were made

negative: No reload-to-undo for major choices.
visions: I see a door you closed that stays closed, and you are glad it does.

neg.signal: enjoys relationships felt before they are understood
neg.implication: Hide the numbers. State is communicated through the world's look, sound and behaviour.
negative: No visible stats, percentages or damage numbers.
visions: I see no numbers at all.

pos.signal: likes stated rules and visible numbers
pos.implication: Show the numbers: odds, counts, meters and stated rules the player can calculate with.

gdv.interface_density: informative: counters, odds and meters are visible

negative: Do not hide the values the player needs to plan with.
visions: I see numbers written plainly on beautiful things, and you counting on them.

neg.implication: A solitary world. Presences may be implied but are never chatty; there is no party to manage.
negative: No mandatory companion.
visions: I see you alone in it, and content.

pos.implication: Put people in it: a handful of distinct characters who notice the player and remember.
negative: Do not make the world empty of people.
visions: I see faces that will know you the second time.

high.implication: Measure and show improvement: times, clean runs, fewer mistakes.

gdv.replayability: improvement: a visible personal best to beat

visions: I see a number that only you care about, going down.

high.signal: plays to find what was not shown
high.implication: Secrets are real: hidden spaces and rules with their own content, not trinkets.

gdv.hidden_information: high: at least three real secrets

visions: I see something waiting on the other side.

high.implication: A small set of collectibles with a visible display that shows the gaps.

gdv.collectibles: yes: a small set, shown on a shelf or case with visible gaps

visions: I see a shelf, and gaps on it, and you cannot leave them.

negative: No collect-a-thon.

high.implication: Upgrades change what is possible, not just numbers.

gdv.progression_structure: a few upgrades, each of which opens something that was closed

visions: I see a power with no top that anyone has found.

high.implication: The player chooses how they look or what they leave behind, and the world addresses them accordingly.

gdv.customization: yes: a visible choice of self or mark, acknowledged by the world

visions: I see you dressed for it, and addressed accordingly.

high.signal: plays to learn what it means
high.implication: A central question is posed early and answered in play, not in a text dump.

gdv.ending_structure: ends on an answer to a question the first minute asked

visions: I see a word in the second column that you will finally be able to read.

high.signal: enjoys the joke and joins in
high.implication: The game is allowed to be funny: comic timing in reactions, item descriptions with jokes, and a world that plays along.

gdv.audiovisual_mood: light and dry; comic timing in animation and text

visions: I see a door that will take your word for it.

negative: Do not lean on jokes.

high.implication: One or two set pieces where the whole screen does something enormous.

gdv.reward_schedule: includes at least one set-piece moment

visions: I see the whole world turning over your head, once.

high.implication: A visible list that can be finished: N of N, shown and satisfying to close.

gdv.collectibles: a finishable catalogue: N of N visible at all times
gdv.ending_structure: a true ending for completing everything

visions: I see seven hollows and seven marbles, and the note it makes.

high.implication: The player builds or arranges something persistent, and the game keeps it.

gdv.secondary_loop: build or arrange something that persists and is used later

visions: I see a thing nobody asked you to make, and it has a name.

high.implication: Give them a rival, a ghost or a score to beat.

gdv.social_structure: a rival or ghost to race; single player

visions: I see someone a step ahead of you on the stairs, laughing.

negative: No leaderboards or versus pressure.

high.implication: Helping is a mechanic: someone needs something, and giving it is play.

gdv.secondary_loop: help someone: carry, fetch, protect or free

visions: I see something small, stuck, and you stopping for it.

high.implication: Unknown outcomes that are usually delightful: boxes, buttons and doors whose results cannot be predicted.
visions: I see a box that rattles, and you buying it instead of the map.

high.implication: The game has seams on purpose: sequence breaks, exploits and rule-lawyering are anticipated and rewarded.

gdv.systemic_interaction: rules can be bent; at least one intended exploit

visions: I see a wall you were not meant to climb, and a note at the top, addressed to you.

negative: Do not require breaking rules to progress.

high.implication: Problems are about position, route and shape.

gdv.camera_perspective: a view that shows the whole spatial problem

high.implication: Problems reward timing and precision; controls are tight and responsive.
The world behaves in patterns that can be read and predicted.
Give clues that jointly determine an answer; let the player prove it.
One scarce resource whose spending is the central decision.
visions: I see an inventory full of things you refuse to use.

high.signal: plays with wording and rules as written
high.implication: Words matter: names, commands or written rules are part of the mechanism.
Objects respond to being tried; combinations do things; nothing explains itself in advance.
Characters have wants that can be learned and used; talking is a tool.

high.signal: finds the best line through known numbers
high.implication: Give known quantities and let the player find the best plan.

high.signal: uses things for what they were not meant for
high.implication: Every object has an off-label use, and the game honours it.
visions: I see a useless thing in your pocket, and the one door it fits.

high.implication: Opposition can always be evaded: stealth, routes and waiting are complete strategies.
Things in the way can be talked to, and asking works.
Opponents and systems can be fooled, baited and played against each other.
Confrontation is available and satisfying; the player can simply push.
The environment can be set up in advance: traps, positions, lures.
Mayhem is a strategy; things fall over in entertaining ways.
One companion follows the player, needs a little care, and matters at the end.

gdv.npc_density: one companion who follows and matters

visions: I see one companion. You will become embarrassingly attached to them.

high.implication: A recurring rival who is fun to lose to and better to beat.
visions: I see someone who says: next time, I pick the course.

high.implication: A few characters reappear and remember what the player did.
Two groups with opposed interests; the player can side, mediate or play them off.

gdv.social_structure: two factions whose quarrel the player can settle or use

high.implication: Characters have routines and needs that can be observed and used.
At least one crowded, noisy place.
A visible other to measure against.
A task that takes two, with an NPC partner.

visions: I see a kettle that has boiled for two.

gdv.audiovisual_mood: deadpan absurd: nonsense treated with complete seriousness
hushed and strange; more implied than shown
dark and tense, with real threat

negative: No horror or jump scares.
Avoid sensory overload.

gdv.narrative_delivery: through a few distinct characters and what they want
environmental: objects, places, signs and records

high.signal: wants to know what happens next

gdv.narrative_delivery: a promise set up early and paid off late

high.signal: likes the story their own actions made

gdv.narrative_delivery: the game records what the player did and shows it back

high.signal: enjoys getting in over their head

gdv.progression_structure: the situation outgrows the player on purpose
capability stays level; the situations change

high.signal: keeps going when nothing says stop

gdv.progression_structure: wild escalation: every use bigger and stranger than the last

visions: I see the floor open, and then the ceiling, and you still reaching.

contradictions.resolution: A mysterious world governed by highly consistent, discoverable rules: nothing is explained and everything is exact.
contradictions.vision: I see rules you will discover before anyone explains them.

contradictions.resolution: Dense small spaces full of secrets rather than a large open world: every screen holds something, and nothing is far.
contradictions.vision: I see a small place with more doors than it has room for.

contradictions.resolution: Secrets found at speed: optional discoveries sit on the fast line and are taken in passing, not searched for.
contradictions.vision: I see you finding things without ever slowing down.

contradictions.resolution: Hard encounters with instant retries and changing conditions: failure costs a second and never the same second twice.
contradictions.vision: I see you dying three times at the same door, and smiling on the fourth.

contradictions.resolution: Story communicated through consequences, environment and mechanics; nothing ever stops play to talk.
contradictions.vision: I see a story told entirely by what happens to you.

contradictions.resolution: Dangerous experiments in a forgiving world: bold actions with spectacular results and a cheap undo.
contradictions.vision: I see you pressing everything, because the world can take it.

contradictions.resolution: A safe world worth combing: no threat on the main path, many secrets, and danger only where the player goes looking.
contradictions.vision: I see you opening every door in a house that will not hurt you.

contradictions.resolution: Clear tools and no assigned goals: a sandbox whose rules are stated and whose purposes are the player's own.
contradictions.vision: I see every tool labelled and no one telling you what to build.

contradictions.resolution: Plan in calm, execute in storms: short preparation phases followed by intense execution of the plan.
contradictions.vision: I see a long breath, and then everything at once.

contradictions.resolution: Style is a build: the expressive choice changes how you play rather than how well.
contradictions.vision: I see you choosing the handsome option and finding it works differently, not worse.

contradictions.resolution: Alone except for one: a single companion in an otherwise empty world.
contradictions.vision: I see one companion. You will become embarrassingly attached to them.

contradictions.resolution: Fragile but dangerous: great power in a body that cannot take a hit.
contradictions.vision: I see you holding something enormous in a very small hand.

contradictions.resolution: One mechanic, bottomless: minimal rules with a high skill ceiling.
contradictions.vision: I see one thing you can do, and no end to how well.

contradictions.resolution: Permanent choices without punishment: the world remembers what was chosen and never how the player failed.
contradictions.vision: I see a world that keeps your decisions and forgets your mistakes.

contradictions.resolution: Novelty with a checklist: every new thing found is logged toward a catalogue that can be finished.
contradictions.vision: I see a book with blank pages, filling.

contradictions.resolution: A guided game that keeps handing the player rules it hopes they will break.
contradictions.vision: I see a sign that says NO, put there for you.

contradictions.resolution: A warm room in a strange house: safety and unease in alternation, each making the other sharper.
contradictions.vision: I see a lit window, and the dark it is lit against.

contradictions.resolution: Informed recklessness: the player can study a danger completely and is then rewarded for walking into it anyway.
contradictions.vision: I see you reading the warning twice, and then lifting the flap.

contradictions.resolution: A systems game with one relationship in it: no dialogue trees, one creature that follows.
contradictions.vision: I see no one talking, and something small keeping up with you.

contradictions.resolution: Power that must be spent to be had: strong one-use abilities, and a game that eventually makes the player use them.
contradictions.vision: I see a power you will save for a moment that almost never comes.

contradictions.resolution: One clear errand that is always visible and never urgent, in a place where every side door is worth opening: the errand waits, and says so.
contradictions.vision: I see one thing you were asked to do, waiting patiently while you open everything else.

contradictions.resolution: The rules are written down and can be studied, and careful reading is exactly how they are broken: the loophole is always in the text.
contradictions.vision: You will read the rules twice. The second time, you will be looking for the gap.

contradictions.resolution: Rule-breaking that cannot cost anything: the game marks clearly what is safe to misuse, and misusing it is where the fun is.
contradictions.vision: I see you breaking something that was built to be broken, and checking first that it was.

contradictions.resolution: A place with no orders and a perfectly honest ledger: do anything at all, and see exactly what it did.
contradictions.vision: Nobody will tell you what to do. Everything will tell you what you did.

contradictions.resolution: Dangerous things can be practised safely first: a rehearsal space, then the real attempt, with the retry free and the stakes chosen.
contradictions.vision: I see you failing where it does not count, until you can do it where it does.

contradictions.resolution: Danger at a deliberate pace: tempting, risky things that wait to be poked, with all the time in the world to decide.
contradictions.vision: There will be something dangerous in the middle of a quiet room, and no clock.

contradictions.resolution: Effort without waiting: the reward is hard to earn and the earning never pauses.
contradictions.vision: I see a hard climb taken at a run.

contradictions.resolution: Deep systems, plainly labelled: every rule is stated in a sentence, and the depth is in how the sentences combine.
contradictions.vision: I see a machine with every part labelled, and you still surprised by what it does.

contradictions.resolution: A populated place that asks nothing: people with their own business, whom the player may join, help or ignore.
contradictions.vision: I see a house full of people, none of whom are waiting for you.

contradictions.resolution: Nonsense with exact rules: the world is absurd and its numbers are honest.
contradictions.vision: I see a ridiculous thing, measured to the inch.

contradictions.resolution: Choices are permanent and none of them can hurt: what is closed stays closed, and nothing closed was needed.
contradictions.vision: I see a door you closed for good, and nothing lost behind it.

contradictions.resolution: The straight road passes through the grand thing: the spectacle is on the critical path, not hidden off it.
contradictions.vision: You will not leave the road. The road goes through the middle of something enormous.

fantasies.reward.mastery: getting it wrong in private until you can do it perfectly
fantasies.reward.discovery: being the first person to understand a place that was not built to be understood
fantasies.reward.collection: filling the last empty place on a shelf
fantasies.reward.power: becoming the most capable thing in the room, and noticing
fantasies.reward.expression: being treated by the world as exactly what you chose to be
fantasies.reward.revelation: finally being able to read the word in the second column
fantasies.reward.humor: being the straight man in a world that is trying to keep a straight face
fantasies.reward.spectacle: standing in the middle of something enormous as it turns
fantasies.reward.creation: leaving a place more yours than you found it
fantasies.reward.competition: arriving one step ahead of someone who is very good
fantasies.reward.cooperation: looking after something small in a place too big for it
fantasies.reward.surprise: opening the box without knowing what is in it
fantasies.reward.transgression: finding out what the machine does when you use it wrong

scope.summary: A pocket game, so that it gets finished. I have not examined these lines. They hold until I change them: tell me in your first reply which you would change, and why.
constraints: Size: a whole game, not a first chapter: 10 to 30 minutes of play in all. One core mechanic and at most two supporting ones.
Engine and platform: Godot 4, 2D, desktop, unless a survey of the machine it is built on argues otherwise.
Art: drawn in code (shapes, lines, palettes, shaders, particles) or built from engine primitives, with the engine's default font. No downloaded or generated assets unless the owner rules on a look.
Audio: none, or synthesised in code. No downloaded audio.
Players: one, offline, keyboard (and mouse if the core verb needs it).
One documented command starts the game from a fresh checkout.
